title: Forward-port the approved live world renderer onto the current product closeout

scope.subject: Forward-port ProceduralPlanets live Planet + PlanetPass into the current product-closeout R3F host while preserving navigation recovery, manual camera takeover and shared world framing

research_summary: Reuse the already-approved LIVE-WORLD-RENDERER-V3-001 architecture and the installed ProceduralPlanets v0.5.1 Planet + PlanetPass subsystem, but forward-port it onto the current product-closeout implementation instead of merging the older renderer branch. Preserve current UniverseCanvas navigation failure recovery, destination routing, manual camera takeover, PLANET_RENDER_RADIUS framing and software-WebGL fallback semantics.

sources.finding: ProceduralPlanets v0.5.1 documents live Planet rendering inside an existing Three scene, logarithmic depth support, impostor LOD, and an EffectComposer path where PlanetPass is inserted immediately after RenderPass.
PlanetPass is a small EffectComposer pass that reuses PlanetRenderer, preserves RenderPass depth, writes linear HDR into the composer buffer, and disposes its renderer.

Pinned MIT YEIS already owns the cross-scale universe/system/body model and native renderer semantics; this task must stay subordinate to that higher-level authority rather than introduce a parallel universe engine.
React Three Fiber can host existing Three Object3D instances through primitive while the application remains responsible for disposal of externally-created objects.
Cosmos is a broader universe-scale renderer candidate with camera-relative coordinates and LOD, but adopting it here would duplicate the already-selected YEIS universe and R3F host.

search_ladder.conclusion: Pinned MIT YEIS remains the chosen higher-level universe solution; Cosmos is also capable but would duplicate universe ownership. Neither should be swapped in merely to repair the close-world visual tier.
The existing React Three Fiber shared Canvas already provides lifecycle, scene access and the single WebGL renderer. Reuse it; do not create a second canvas or renderer authority.

ProceduralPlanets v0.5.1 already ships the exact live Planet and PlanetPass subsystem needed, including composer integration, depth compositing, LOD/impostors and logarithmic-depth compatibility. Upgrade the existing baked use to this live path.

The existing CinematicPipeline already uses Three EffectComposer with RenderPass, bloom and OutputPass, so PlanetPass can be inserted into the established chain rather than creating custom post-processing glue.

candidates.name: Pinned YEIS MIT renderer as the complete world stack
candidates.reason: Correct higher-level authority and valuable for the subsequent System renderer, but replacing the close-world tier with its full physical-km camera/body pipeline is a much larger integration than needed for the immediate visual defect.

candidates.name: Cosmos universe renderer
candidates.reason: Broad visual coverage but would introduce a second universe/camera stack next to YEIS and duplicate the adopted R3F integration.

candidates.name: Existing React Three Fiber shared Canvas
candidates.source: React Three Fiber already in project
candidates.reason: Keeps one renderer/canvas and lets the live Planet object coexist with the existing HUD, camera and transition lifecycle.

candidates.name: ProceduralPlanets v0.5.1 Planet + PlanetPass
candidates.reason: Already installed and already adopted for world generation; the live tier directly fixes close-up terrain/atmosphere/cloud quality and plugs into the existing EffectComposer without a new engine.

coverage_matrix.capability: Close world surface quality at approach/orbit scale
coverage_matrix.decision: Use ProceduralPlanets live terrain/atmosphere/cloud rendering for the current selected-world tier while retaining YEIS as universe authority.

coverage_matrix.capability: Reuse existing post-processing and shared Canvas without a second WebGL owner
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep R3F and insert PlanetPass into the current EffectComposer immediately after RenderPass.
Reuse ProceduralPlanets visibility culling and impostor LOD, then map existing quality mode to live renderer parameters only where necessary.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve navigation/content authority and deep-link semantics
coverage_matrix.decision: Renderer receives the already-selected PlanetDefinition only; Search/Places/Canvas/deep-link/Journey remain unchanged.

coverage_matrix.capability: Preserve post-freeze product navigation, manual camera takeover and shared world framing while adding live rendering
coverage_matrix.decision: Forward-port only the live renderer path into the current files; do not replace current UniverseCanvas contracts or hard-code a separate world radius.

decision.rationale: Keep the current product-closeout R3F Canvas, navigation/camera contracts and shared PLANET_RENDER_RADIUS. Reuse the previously approved ProceduralPlanets live Planet + PlanetPass subsystem as a forward-port, with delayed warm-in and hardware-aware fallback. Do not merge the older renderer branch wholesale.

higher_level_tradeoffs.reason: YEIS remains the higher-level selected engine and will be reused for the System layer next, but pulling its full physical-km camera/body rendering stack into the close-world phase first would enlarge the change while leaving an already-adopted live planet subsystem unused.
Cosmos is broad enough to solve the visual tier, but replacing YEIS/R3F universe ownership solely for this gap would duplicate current navigation, content binding and runtime work.

decision.fallback: If the forward-port fails build or live readiness on the current closeout baseline, retain the existing lightweight world path and keep the pinned YEIS native system renderer closure available while investigating upstream compatibility; do not regress navigation/camera contracts.
